content_html_sanitized:
Recently, I have written about the misrepresentation of the meaning of the rescheduling of cannabis from Schedule 1 to Schedule 3 classification.

 

See

Very Simple Example of the Incompetence of Reporting on Marijuana Prohibition

 

Cannabis being in Schedule 1 means that it officially has no medical use. Moving it to Schedule 3 would mean that it has recognized medical uses.

 

From the website of the American Cancer Society:

● Pain

● Nausea and vomiting

● Anorexia (loss of appetite)

● Stress and anxiety

● Sleep problems

 

Prohibitionists complain that rescheduling would mean that cannabis is “less dangerous”.

 

Yes, but (basic grammar lesson.) Less dangerous than what? “Less dangerous” isn’t some metaphysical concept, like degrees of holiness.

 

From Merriam Webster: “Less” is comparative of LITTLE.

See Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It

 

So, are the Prohibitionists really saying that cannabis is as dangerous as fentanyl in Schedule 2?

 

In 2023 alone, around 72,776 people in the United States died from a drug overdose that involved fentanyl.

 

Such is the degraded quality of the public discourse, and  journalism specifically, that we cannot even get a grammatically accurate description of an important public health issue.

 

See MMJ International Has Posted Another Important Story: DEA Unconstitutional Marijuana Playbook: How the DEA Is Repeating the DOL's Mistakes Against MMJ BioPharma
